## Is Shotcut free for commercial use?

Yes, because the software is made available under the GPLv3 license, it
supports [The Free Software Definition](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html),
which includes:

> The freedom to run the program as you wish, for any purpose (freedom 0).

## Which Export preset should I use?

It all depends; that is why there are so many of them! But here are some
suggestions:

- Upload to a video-sharing web site: `H.264 High Profile` or `YouTube`
- Extract the audio: `Ogg Vorbis`, `FLAC` (lossless with compression), or good old `MP3`
- Save to an intermediate file to use with another tool: `DNxHR HQ` or
`ProRes 422` \- really depends on what the other tool accepts
- Put onto my own web site: `WebM` and/or `Default` (moderate quality H.264)
- Screen recording (Linux only): `intermediate/MJPEG`
- Capture from SDI/HDMI: `intermediate/ProRes 422` if your system can handle it,
otherwise `intermediate/MPEG-2`

#### About

Shotcut is a free, open source, cross-platform video editor for Windows, Mac and Linux. Major features include support for a wide range of formats; no import required meaning native timeline editing; Blackmagic Design support for input and preview monitoring; and resolution support to 4k.

Free and Open Source Video Editor

Asset Management

Take control of your edit with a flexible non-linear workflow, [multicam](https://docs.kdenlive.org/project_and_asset_management/project_settings/proxy_settings.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features) and [3-point editing](https://docs.kdenlive.org/cutting_and_assembling/editing.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features#point-editing).

Screenshots collage of Kdenlive widgets related to audio.

Can you hear the difference? Shape your soundtrack with powerful [mixers](https://docs.kdenlive.org/effects_and_filters/audio.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features#audio-mixer), built-in [voiceover recording](https://docs.kdenlive.org/effects_and_filters/audio.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features#audio-recording), and an [audio spectrum](https://docs.kdenlive.org/user_interface/menu/view_menu.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features#scope-audio-spectrum) that lets you see exactly what you’re hearing.

Add smooth [transitions](https://docs.kdenlive.org/compositing/transitions.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features) between clips and combine layers with flexible [compositions](https://docs.kdenlive.org/compositing/compositions.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features) to create polished, dynamic sequences.

Create professional [subtitles](https://docs.kdenlive.org/effects_and_filters/subtitles.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features) with [automatic transcription](https://docs.kdenlive.org/effects_and_filters/speech_to_text.html?mtm_campaign=kdenliveorg_front_features), advanced layering and styling.

The free version works with virtually all 8-bit video formats at up to 60fps in resolutions as high as Ultra HD 3840 x 2160. The free version includes multi-user collaboration and HDR grading!

It also supports 10-bit video up to 120 frames per second and resolutions beyond 4K.

FFmpeg is licensed under the [GNU Lesser\ General Public License (LGPL) version 2.1](http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.html) or later. If those parts get used the GPL applies to all of FFmpeg.

Note that FFmpeg is not available under any other licensing terms, especially not proprietary/commercial ones, not even in exchange for payment.

Q: Bottom line: Should I be worried about patent issues if I use FFmpeg?

A: Are you a private user working with FFmpeg for your own personal purposes? If so, there is remarkably little reason to be concerned. Are you using FFmpeg in a commercial software product?

A: You might have a problem here. These companies found out that once you start trying to make money from patented technologies, the owners of the patents will come after their licensing fees. Notably, MPEG LA is vigilant and diligent about collecting for MPEG-related technologies.
